passages.iast: sarvaṃ ca nāmarūpādi sadātmanaiva satyaṃ vikārajātaṃ svastvanṛtameva
passages.english: All name-and-form and the like is true only with Sat as its Self; the class of modifications is untrue in its own right.
passages.grammar: sarvaṃ is the subject. ca links the series. nāmarūpādi is a collective nominal expression, 'name-and-form and the like'. sadātmanaiva is sat-ātmanā eva in sandhi: 'with Sat alone as its Self'. satyaṃ and anṛtam are the opposed predicates. vikārajātaṃ is the arisen class of modifications. svastvanṛtameva is svatas tu anṛtam eva in sandhi, an adverbial exclusion: 'however, in its own right, untrue'.

words.gloss: with Sat alone as its Self

words.morph: nom. sg. neut. collective noun from vikāra + jāta
svatas + tu + anṛtam + eva in sandhi

passages.english: Ultimate non-otherness from the cause is the effect’s absence when the cause is excluded.
passages.grammar: kāraṇāt is apādāna, ablative of separation: 'from the cause'. paramārthataḥ is an adverbial ablative, 'ultimately / in ultimate truth'. ’nanyatvam is the abstract noun 'non-otherness'. vyatirekeṇa is an instrumental of exclusion: 'by exclusion, apart from'. abhāvaḥ is the nominal predicate 'absence'. kāryasya is a genitive dependent on abhāvaḥ: 'of the effect'.

passages.iast: daivī devasya mameśvarasya viṣṇoḥ svabhāva-bhūtā hi yasmād eṣā yathoktā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā
passages.english: This divine māyā of mine, made of the guṇas, is of the nature of the Lord Viṣṇu and is hard to cross.
passages.grammar: daivī is nominative singular feminine. devasya, mameśvarasya, and viṣṇoḥ are genitives of relation. svabhāva-bhūtā is a compound participial adjective, 'become / constituted as its own nature'. hi is emphatic. yasmād introduces the reason. eṣā and yathoktā are nominative feminine forms referring to māyā. guṇa-mayī is a karmadhāraya compound, 'made of the guṇas'. duratyayā is a feminine adjective, 'hard to cross'.

passages.iast:
mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā
mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ
na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram
bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ
passages.english: All this world is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form. All beings are situated in me, yet I am not situated in them. And yet beings are not situated in me: behold my divine yoga. I bear beings but am not established in them; my Self is the sustainer and generator of beings.
passages.grammar: mayā is instrumental, the agent of pervasion. tatam is the past passive participle 'pervaded'. idaṃ sarvaṃ jagat is the full extent of the pervaded world. avyakta-mūrtinā qualifies the mode of presence. mat-sthāni uses a locative relation, 'situated in me'. teṣu and mat-sthāni are reciprocally opposed in the two verses. bhūta-bhṛt, bhūta-sthaḥ, and bhūta-bhāvanaḥ are nominal epithets that preserve non-involvement while asserting sustaining power.

passages.english: Between Īśvara and jīva there is a difference of guise and cognition; in their nature as Being, the reality is one alone.
passages.grammar: īśa-jīvayor is a genitive dual: 'of Īśa and jīva'. veṣa-dhī-bhidā is a compound nominal, 'difference of guise and cognition'. sat-svabhāvataḥ is an ablative of respect / cause: 'by nature as Being'. vastu is the neutral noun 'reality / thing'. kevalam is the limiting adjective 'alone'.

passages.iast:
jīveśvarabhidā caiva jaḍeśvarabhidā tathā /
jīvabhedo mithaścaiva jaḍajīvabhidā tathā /
mithaśca jaḍabhedo yaḥ prapañco bhedapañcakaḥ //
so 'yaṃ satyo hyanādiśca sādiścennāśamāpnuyāt /
dvaitaṃ na vidyata iti tasmādajñānināṃ matam //
passages.english: {0:Difference between the jīva and Lord}, {1:and indeed}, {2:difference between the insentient and Lord}, {3:likewise}; {4:difference among jīvas}, {5:mutually and indeed}; {6:difference between the insentient and jīva}, {7:likewise}; {8:mutually}, {9:difference among insentient things}, {10:which} {11:world-manifold} [is] {12:the fivefold aggregate of differences}. {13:That} {14:this} [world-manifold is] {15:real}, {16:indeed}, {17:beginningless}, {18:and}; {20:if} [it were] {19:possessed of a beginning}, [it] {22:would attain} {21:destruction}. {23:Duality} {24:not} {25:exists}, {26:thus}; {27:therefore}, [this is] {28:of non-knowers} {29:the view}.
passages.grammar: The passage is built from five relational compounds naming the five bhedas Madhva treats as real. I have kept the compounds as single clickable units where that preserves the transmitted form; the internal vigraha is noted in the word cards. The phrase sādiḥ is slightly compressed in the transmitted sandhi; it is read here as “having a beginning.”

words.gloss: and mutually / and likewise among themselves

words.note: The transmitted sandhi is compressed; the intended sense is ‘if it had a beginning’.

passages.iast:
śuddhaḥ sākṣī yadā siddho duḥkhitvaṃ vāryate katham /
upajīvyapramāṇaṃ tad bhedagrāhakam eva hi /
ato jīveśayor bhedaḥ śrutisāmarthyasusthiraḥ //
tathāpi tu cidānandapūrvāstatsadṛśā guṇāḥ /
sārasvarūpamasyāpi muktāvapyavaśiṣyate //
ato 'bhedavadevaitāḥ śrutayaḥ pravadanti hi /
paurāṇāni ca vākyāni sādṛśyābhedasaṃśrayāt //
sādṛśyācca pradhānatvāt svātantryādapicābhidām /
āhurīśena jīvasya na svarūpābhidāṃ kvacit //
passages.english: When the pure witness is established, how can the condition of being a sufferer be denied? That means of knowledge on which one relies apprehends difference. Therefore the difference between jīva and Lord is firmly established by the force of scripture. Yet qualities beginning with consciousness and bliss still remain as similar to that [Lord], and the essential nature of this [jīva] remains even in liberation. Therefore these scriptural statements speak as if of non-difference. The Purāṇic statements do so too, because they rest on similarity-grounded non-difference. And because of similarity, primacy, and sovereignty, they apply Lord-language to the jīva, but never essential identity.
passages.grammar: This passage runs in two parts in the article: the first establishes the witness and the firmness of difference; the second explains why abheda-language can still be used without granting svarūpa-abheda. Several compounds are dense; where a compact reading is uncertain I have kept the transmitted form as a single unit and expanded the sense in the word gloss or compound vigraha.

words.gloss: the underlying / relied-on means of knowledge
firmly established by the force of scripture
those beginning with consciousness and bliss
because they rest on similarity-grounded non-difference

words.note: The transmitted form is compact; the point is the application of īśvara-language.

words.gloss: by the Lord / with respect to the Lord

upajīvyapramāṇaṃ tad bhedagrāhakam eva hi /

passages.grammar: This is the hermeneutic half of the locus. The key contrast is between abhedavat language and svarūpābhidā, which Madhva explicitly denies. The compact clauses are preserved as transmitted; the English makes the inferential structure explicit.

because they rest on similarity-grounded non-difference

passages.english: {0:Of the Lord and the living being}: {1:a difference of guise-cognition}; {2:with respect to nature as Sat}, {3:reality} {4:alone}.
passages.grammar: Two nominal clauses; no finite verb is present. The internal relation in veṣa-dhī-bhidā is genuinely underdetermined by the verse alone and is left marked as such rather than silently settled.

words.note: The verse alone does not decide between 'difference in cognition of guise' and a compressed co-ordinate relation; no decisive vigraha is invented.

passages.iast:
svatantraṃ paratantraṃ ca prameyaṃ dvividhaṃ matam /
svatantro bhagavān viṣṇur nirdoṣākhila-sad-guṇaḥ //
...
ya etat paratantraṃ tu sarvam eva hareḥ sadā /
vaśam ity eva jānāti saṃsārān mucyate hi saḥ //
passages.devanagari:
स्वतन्त्रं परतन्त्रं च प्रमेयं द्विविधं मतम् ।
स्वतन्त्रो भगवान् विष्णुर्निर्दोषाखिलसद्गुणः ॥
...
य एतत् परतन्त्रं तु सर्वम् एव हरेः सदा ।
वशम् इत्येव जानाति संसारान् मुच्यते हि सः ॥
passages.english: The knowable is held to be twofold: independent and dependent. The independent is Bhagavān Viṣṇu, faultless and endowed with every good quality. ... Whoever knows that all this dependent reality is always under Hari's control is released from saṃsāra.
passages.grammar: Verse 1 defines the ontological split between svatantra and paratantra. Verse 13 turns that dependence into the liberation condition: knowledge of Hari's control over all the dependent is itself emancipating.

words.karaka: first member of the knowable's twofold division
second member of the knowable's twofold division

words.gloss: faultless, with every true good quality

passages.iast: na hi brahmātmaikyasya yāthārthyaṃ tatpakṣe / advaitahāneḥ svarūpātireke / anatireke svaprakāśatvād ātmanaḥ siddhasādhanatā
passages.devanagari: न हि ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्य याथार्थ्यं तत्पक्षे । अद्वैतहानेः स्वरूपातिरेके । अनतिरेके स्वप्रकाशत्वाद् आत्मनः सिद्धसाधनता ।
passages.english: For the factual correctness of Brahman–Self identity does not obtain on that position. If there is otherness of intrinsic nature, non-duality is lost; if there is no such otherness, then, because the Self is self-luminous, the claim proves what is already established.
passages.grammar: The source is a compressed prose dilemma, not a full conditional sentence. The three alternatives are stated elliptically and the omitted copula belongs to the argument's context.

words.gloss: in the case of being other than intrinsic nature
the fault of proving what is already established

passages.iast:
nānyadanyatvamāpannaṃ kvacid dṛṣṭaṃ kathañcana /
ato jīvasya na brahmabhāvaḥ syād dhi kadācana //
passages.devanagari:
नान्यदन्यत्वमापन्नं क्वचिद् दृष्टं कथञ्चन ।
अतो जीवस्य न ब्रह्मभावः स्याद् धि कदाचन ॥
passages.english: No other entity having acquired non-otherness is seen anywhere in any manner. Therefore the jīva can never have Brahman-nature at any time.
passages.grammar: The first half is a compressed denial of any observed case where an already other entity has acquired non-otherness. The second half states the universal conclusion for the jīva.

words.gloss: no other entity having acquired non-otherness
words.note: Saṃhitā combines na + anyat + ananyatvam āpannam.
